tagline: Andaman's mainland gateway — limestone-island demand, boat-only nodes.
summary: Krabi is the Andaman mainland hub feeding a dense archipelago — Phi Phi, Hong, Poda, Chicken Island and the cliff-ringed Railay peninsula — plus the busy Ao Nang resort strip. Its airport has grown past three million passengers a year, and much of its signature geography is road-inaccessible and reachable only by water, so the boat trip is not an add-on here — it is the only way in. Today every leg runs on diesel longtails and speedboats: noisy, fume-heavy and wake-churning in waters where reef tours and beach resorts are the whole draw. A quiet, smooth, zero-wake foiling shuttle turns the water transfer itself into part of the premium Andaman experience, and pairs Krabi with Phuket across the ~18 nm corridor.

use_cases.title: Ao Nang ↔ Railay premium beach shuttle
use_cases.body: A smooth, near-silent hop to the cliff-ringed Railay peninsula — the only beach in the region reachable solely by water. Where today guests wedge into a wet, noisy longtail, a foiling shuttle delivers them dry, calm and on their own schedule.

use_cases.title: Krabi ↔ Phi Phi island transfer
use_cases.body: A direct foiling crossing from the Krabi mainland to the Phi Phi archipelago that flies above the Andaman chop, arriving day-trippers and resort guests fresh rather than rattled by a diesel speedboat. The smooth, low-wake ride also fits the conservation rules tightening across the national-park waters.

use_cases.title: Krabi ↔ Phuket Andaman cross-corridor
use_cases.body: A fast water link across the ~18 nm Andaman corridor connecting the two biggest Andaman gateways without the long road detour around the bay. It knits Krabi's island demand to Phuket's air and resort base into one coastal network.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Krabi mixes ultra-short captive hops with mid-range corridors that all sit inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — Ao Nang↔Railay (~2 nm), Krabi↔Phi Phi (~23 nm) and the Krabi↔Phuket cross-corridor (~18 nm) — with multi-operator piers at Klong Jilad and Ao Nang that ease shore-charging siting and the boat-only nodes removing any road-modal competition.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range, with no charging-infrastructure dependency, extends the Andaman network down the coast — Phuket, Phang Nga, Koh Lanta and the outer islands — and bridges open-water legs that island grid power could not yet support for all-electric charging.

competitive_landscape: Dense longtail + speedboat operators (Ao Nang Longtail Boat Club controls Railay access); all diesel/2-stroke, noise- and wake-heavy — a quiet electric shuttle is a clean differentiator.
seasonality: Peak: Nov-Apr dry season. SW monsoon May-Oct raises Andaman swell; range-gate cross-corridors, keep short captive hops year-round.
regulatory_note: Thai cabotage; Marine Department domestic licensing. Railay longtail cartel is a real access-politics factor — partner-of-record / local-operator structure advised.
